item.title: Rosso asks what comes next
item.description: Papua New Guinea must now look beyond its first 51 years of independence and decide what it wants for the generations ahead, Deputy Prime Minister John Rosso says. Rosso, who is also the Lae MP, was the principal guest at Lae’s 51st Independence anniversary celebration at Sir Ignatius Kilage Stadium on Wednesday.
item.content:encoded:
Papua New Guinea must now look beyond its first 51 years of independence and decide what it wants for the generations ahead, Deputy Prime Minister John Rosso says.

Rosso, who is also the Lae MP, was the principal guest at Lae’s 51st Independence anniversary celebration at Sir Ignatius Kilage Stadium on Wednesday.

In his speech, Rosso reflected on 16 September 1975 and his memories of watching the Australian flag come down and the Papua New Guinean flag rise.

He paid tribute to the leaders who guided the country to independence, including Grand Chief Sir Michael Somare and Sir Julius Chan.

Rosso said Papua New Guinea had achieved independence peacefully despite its many languages, cultures and communities.

He said that unity remained important as the country entered its next 50 years.

“What do we want for the next 50 years?” Rosso asked.

He said Independence Day should be more than a celebration. It should also be a time for Papua New Guineans to think about the country they want to leave for their children and grandchildren.

Rosso also remembered former Lae MP and Morobe leader Songar Luthawake, whose first anniversary of death falls this week.

He urged Papua New Guineans to remember the sacrifices of earlier generations while taking responsibility for the country’s future.

item.title: West Sepik challenged to reset as PNG celebrates 51st Independence
item.description: As Papua New Guinea celebrates its 51st Independence Anniversary, West Sepik Province has been challenged to reset and refocus for the next 50 years. The call was made by West Sepik Provincial Administrator, Jacob Areman, during the 51st Independence flag-raising ceremony at Pope Francis Oval in Vanimo.
item.content:encoded:
As Papua New Guinea celebrates its 51st Independence Anniversary, West Sepik Province has been challenged to reset and refocus for the next 50 years.

The call was made by West Sepik Provincial Administrator, Jacob Areman, during the 51st Independence flag-raising ceremony at Pope Francis Oval in Vanimo.

The ceremony was officiated by members of the three disciplinary forces - the Royal PNG Constabulary, PNG Defence Force and Correctional Service.

Mr. Areman delivered his address under the provincial theme: "Sharing Our Vision, Admitting Our Challenges and Resetting for Our Future."

He said West Sepik has shared the same vision with the rest of the country and has contributed significantly to national development over the past 50 years.

He said the province has produced human resource leaders, bureaucrats, foreign service officers, medical professionals and contributed to economic growth through the forestry sector.

However, the Provincial Administrator admitted that despite these contributions, the province itself continues to struggle.

"Though West Sepik has contributed well to the country's development, the province itself has been struggling with major infrastructure developments such as poor road conditions, water and sanitation, electricity, health and education," he said.

He added that with no major cash crops or industries to generate internal revenue, the province depends entirely on National Government grants, which often affects service delivery.

"These have been the province's and the country's major challenges in the last 51 years. For West Sepik, though we face these challenges, we have come a long way."

Mr. Areman said it is now time for West Sepik to reset, refocus and rebuild for the next 50 years.

He reminded the people that the province's long-term vision is to transform Vanimo into a City, Aitape into an Industrial Hub, and the Vanimo-Green Corridor into a Free Trade Zone for both West Sepik and Papua New Guinea.

He urged all citizens, including elites and leaders of West Sepik, to work together and focus on developing the province.

item.content:encoded:
As Papua New Guinea marks its 51 years of Indepdence a lesson in traditional Chinese culture has offered international journalists in Bejing China a different perspective on the role of language, broadcasting, and journalism in preserving knowledge and cultural identity.

As part of their training in China, the journalists were introduced to the ancient practice of rubbing, used to reproduce inscriptions and passed down texts before modern printing became widespread.

That lesson unexpectedly connects to Papua New Guinea's own experience. Since independence, broadcasting in local languages has helped communities access information in familiar, meaningful ways.

The National Broadcasting Corporation of Papua New Guinea has continued that role. From radio to establishing of local language TV news early this year 2026, preserving language through modern journalism.

While tools change, the goal remains, carrying stories forward, so future generations can hear them.

item.title: Pokanis hails 51 years of bilateral ties with Philippines
item.description: Papua New Guinea’s Ambassador to the Philippines, Stephen Pokanis, has extended warm independence greetings to both nations while celebrating 51 years of strong bilateral relations and economic partnership. Speaking on the country’s 51st Independence Anniversary, Pokanis acknowledged the Government and people of the Republic of the Philippines as the first international community to formally recog
item.content:encoded:
Papua New Guinea’s Ambassador to the Philippines, Stephen Pokanis, has extended warm independence greetings to both nations while celebrating 51 years of strong bilateral relations and economic partnership.

Speaking on the country’s 51st Independence Anniversary, Pokanis acknowledged the Government and people of the Republic of the Philippines as the first international community to formally recognise PNG’s independence on Sept 16, 1975 .

"Since then, our two governments have established diplomatic and economic ties coinciding with the Trade and Investment Partnership Agreement and established a Joint Economic and Trade Committee to boost cooperation," Pokanis said .

He said key areas of ongoing collaboration include agriculture, fisheries technology transfer, aquaculture, manufacturing, and air services.

Current trade between the two countries sees PNG exporting major commodities such as copper ore and frozen fish, while importing processed goods and food items from the Philippines .

Pokanis said the growing people-to-people connections, has paved way for more than 38,000 Filipinos who currently reside and work in Papua New Guinea, forming the nation's largest international community.

"Filipino professionals are contributing expansively to Papua New Guinea’s healthcare, education, business, mining, gas and oil industries, and infrastructure development," he said .

He expressed confidence in the continuing growth of the relationship, praying for ongoing prosperity and successful friendship between both countries .

item.title: 17 escape in Goroka cell breach
item.description: Seventeen prisoners escaped from the Goroka Police Station cell lockup on Monday night while officers were finalising security plans for major upcoming events. The breach occurred around 8pm, during a period when police personnel, including the station commander, were actively working on operational preparations for the Goroka Show and 51st Independence Day celebrations.
item.content:encoded:
Seventeen prisoners escaped from the Goroka Police Station cell lockup on Monday night while officers were finalising security plans for major upcoming events.

The breach occurred around 8pm, during a period when police personnel, including the station commander, were actively working on operational preparations for the Goroka Show and 51st Independence Day celebrations.

Eastern Highlands provincial police commander Chief Supt Albert Beli expressed shock over the incident, describing it as unprecedented in his police career.

“This is something I did not expect and have never experienced in my line of duty before,” Chief Supt Beli said.

He confirmed that a thorough investigation into how the escape occurred is currently underway.

Chief Supt Beli commended the quick response of the Goroka Taskforce unit and duty officers, who managed to recapture eight of the escapees that night. Nine remain at large.

Following an operational briefing yesterday morning, he assured the public that police will utilize all available resources to track down the remaining fugitives.

He appealed to the families of the escapees to report any information regarding their whereabouts to the police and urged the general public to exercise extra caution while the nine suspects remain at large.

item.title: Bundaira prison receives food rations to compliment independence celebrations
item.description: As Papua New Guinea celebrates its 51st Independence, inmates at the Bundaira Correctional Institution in Kainantu, Eastern Highlands, will also mark the occasion and take time to reflect on their lives. Eastern Highlands governor Simon Sia visited the prison to present food rations, complementing the inmates' celebrations and reminding them that they are not forgotten by society.
item.content:encoded:
As Papua New Guinea celebrates its 51st Independence, inmates at the Bundaira Correctional Institution in Kainantu, Eastern Highlands, will also mark the occasion and take time to reflect on their lives.

Eastern Highlands governor Simon Sia visited the prison to present food rations, complementing the inmates' celebrations and reminding them that they are not forgotten by society.

Governor Sia urged the prisoners to use the Independence period to reflect on their actions and focus on how they can better themselves for their families and the country.

Bundaira Correctional Institution commanding officer Laka Gaoma thanked Sia for the visit and the generous donation during the national celebrations.

Speaking on behalf of the inmates, prisoners' representative David Tony said they were humbled that the governor took time out of his busy schedule to visit them.

Tony added that while the rest of the country celebrates the 51st Independence in a grand fashion, the inmates will celebrate in their own small way and reflect on their personal rehabilitation.

The donation included bags of rice, cartons of tinned fish, noodles, soap, meat, and K1,000 in cash to support their long weekend festivities.

item.title: Lae remembers war on Independence Day
item.description: On the day Papua New Guinea marked 51 years as an independent nation, Lae also paused to remember a defining moment in its wartime history – the liberation of the city from Japanese occupation 83 years ago. The 83rd anniversary of the Liberation of Lae was commemorated on Wednesday at the 7th Australian Division Memorial Primary School at Situm, bringing together Papua New Guinean and Australian r
item.content:encoded:
On the day Papua New Guinea marked 51 years as an independent nation, Lae also paused to remember a defining moment in its wartime history – the liberation of the city from Japanese occupation 83 years ago.

The 83rd anniversary of the Liberation of Lae was commemorated on Wednesday at the 7th Australian Division Memorial Primary School at Situm, bringing together Papua New Guinean and Australian representatives, defence personnel, students and members of the community.

Australian Consul-General Brenton Kanowski said holding the commemoration on Independence Day was a reminder of the shared history between Papua New Guinea and Australia and the relationship that has developed since the Second World War.

The liberation of Lae on 16 September 1943 followed a major Allied offensive, with Australian forces advancing on the city from several directions.

Kanowski paid tribute to the Australian, Papua New Guinean, American and other Allied forces who fought in the campaign, as well as local people whose support and resilience contributed to the liberation.

He also remembered those who were killed, wounded or whose lives were permanently changed by the war. But 83 years after the fighting ended, Kanowski said the significance of the anniversary extends beyond the battlefield.

“It is also a story of partnership between Australians and Papua New Guineans, forged in difficult circumstances and strengthened over generations,” he said.

That relationship has continued through decades of cooperation in defence, education, health, economic development and people-to-people links.

Kanowski said it was particularly meaningful to remember the liberation on the same day Papua New Guinea celebrates its Independence. In 1943, the people involved in the liberation could not have known that three decades later Papua New Guinea would become an independent nation.

Today, Papua New Guinea and Australia stand as sovereign neighbours and partners, with their relationship shaped in part by the shared experiences of the war.

Speaking to students at the commemoration, Kanowski said remembering the past was also about looking towards the future.

“History is not simply about looking back,” he said. “It is about understanding the sacrifices of those who came before us and drawing inspiration from them as we build a better future.”

The ceremony brought together two important dates in Papua New Guinea’s history – the liberation of Lae in 1943 and the country’s independence in 1975.

For those gathered at Situm, the anniversary was a reminder of the lives lost during the war and the generations that followed to build a free and independent Papua New Guinea.

Lest we forget. Happy 51st Independence Day, Papua New Guinea.

item.title: Police show strength as WHP observes quiet independence
item.description: There may be no major provincial Independence Day celebration in Western Highlands this year, but police presence around Mt Hagen City is clearly visible. Western Highlands police convoyed around the city and surrounding areas, reminding people that the laws of the country remain in force even as the province observes Independence Day quietly.
item.content:encoded:
There may be no major provincial Independence Day celebration in Western Highlands this year, but police presence around Mt Hagen City is clearly visible.

Western Highlands police convoyed around the city and surrounding areas, reminding people that the laws of the country remain in force even as the province observes Independence Day quietly.

Western Highlands Provincial Police Commander Chief Superintendent John Sagom said police will be out in full force to maintain peace and protect people and property.

“We want our people to celebrate Independence peacefully. There is no reason for anyone to break the law or cause problems for other people," Sagom said.

Sagom said the quiet approach to this year’s Independence Day should not be seen as a reason for people to become careless.

He urged everyone, especially young people, to behave responsibly and avoid activities that could lead to fights, destruction of property or other offences.

“Police will be out there. We are ready to respond to any situation, but we also want our people to do the right thing and stay away from trouble," the PPC said.

The police presence will also give public confidence as people move around Mt Hagen City and surrounding communities.

PPC Sagom elaborated that police will continue their normal operations and will not tolerate people taking advantage of the public holiday to break the law.

“Independence belongs to all of us. Let us respect our country by respecting the law, respecting each other and keeping our communities peaceful.”

item.title: Works Dept opens K7.8m Mirisim Haus
item.description: The Department of Works and Highways has officially opened its new K7.8 million office building, naming it Mirisim Haus in honour of former minister, the late Solan Mirisim.

item.description: A beer shop operating in the heart of Lae city was open for business today despite a liquor ban imposed ahead of Papua New Guinea’s 51st Independence celebrations.
